frames.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve animation pose.
Create ONE Crooked Witch animation frame, NOT a sheet. The supplied v4_02 approved base is the SOLE visual reference and definitive eye, face, hairstyle, costume and staff design. Keep exactly its moderately open violet almond eye, upper eyelash silhouette and expression; do not round or enlarge the eye, do not narrow it into a sleepy slit. Preserve its nose, mouth, face profile and head angle.
Preserve intricate deep purple/gold embroidery, ivory layered skirt, silver curled hair, broad bent purple hat, crystal ornaments, tall dark boots, and the exact ornate dark/gold staff with violet crystal and same number of parts. Detailed crisp pixel-art style exactly like the reference.
Same 1254x1254 square canvas, same camera scale and body/weapon dimensions, same hip center, full body and entire staff inside, ample transparent margins. Grounded animation in place: do not translate the character through the scene. Preserve support-foot ground baseline from reference. Camera is fixed. Pose changes can naturally move knees and shoulders, never rescale the character.
The anatomical RIGHT arm is near camera: visible right shoulder leads to the FOREGROUND sleeve, bent elbow and forearm ACROSS FRONT of waist, right hand alone grips the staff at the SAME shaft point in all frames. Fingers wrap shaft, thumb opposing fingers. The left arm is far side, behind torso, mostly occluded, empty hand peeks near far hip. Near RIGHT leg stays in front of far LEFT leg at crossings even while feet alternate front/back positions in the walking direction. Exactly two arms/two legs. No side swapping.
Preserve the exact same character identity, body height, head size, shoulder width,
limb proportions, weapon size, camera distance, foot position and lighting as the reference.
Right-facing three-quarter side view, full body and the entire weapon inside the frame,
flat transparent background, no shadow, no text, no border, no scenery.
Centering and framing are positioning choices only: never zoom, scale, stretch or shrink the
character to center it or to fit the full body/weapon. This applies whether the weapon is raised,
lowered or held horizontally. If the weapon makes the silhouette taller or wider, keep the
character and weapon scale fixed and expand the canvas/margins or adjust the framing instead.
If the canonical runtime frame still cannot contain the full weapon at the fixed scale, stop and
ask the user; do not shrink the character or crop the weapon.
Correct near/far layering: the near arm and near leg are in front of the torso; the far arm
and far leg stay behind it. The weapon is held by the same RIGHT hand with a believable one-handed grip around
the shaft; fingers wrap the shaft, and the hand/weapon do not intersect the torso, head, legs,
hair or clothing. No interpenetration, no merged or extra limbs, no floating parts, and no duplicated weapon.
Only change the pose: IDLE frame 01 of 00..03, gentle inhale. Both boots are planted at exactly the base stance. Lift chest/near shoulder only a few pixels in a natural small breath. Right elbow and hand remain steady, staff stays at reference angle. Hair tips and lower robe edges trail subtly backward, far empty left hand rests loosely at far hip. No walking, no floating, no spell, no blink.
